checklist.text: The lint rule error kind string must be exactly `action-pinning`.
The rule checks step-level action `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule checks job-level reusable workflow `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule is configured via an `action-pinning` config section.
The config section has a `level` field.
The `level` field accepts the value `major-minor`.
The `level` field accepts the value `semver`.
The `level` field accepts the value `commit-sha`.
Level `major-minor` requires vMAJOR.MINOR format.
Level `semver` requires vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format including prerelease.
Level `commit-sha` requires full 40-character lowercase hex SHA.
The default level when none is specified is `semver`.
The levels are ordered by increasing strictness: a ref satisfying a stricter level also satisfies any less strict requirement.
Setting `action-pinning: null` keeps the rule disabled.
Setting `action-pinning: {}` enables the rule with defaults.
Local refs starting with `./` are skipped (not flagged).

checklist.adverse_condition: the uses reference begins with 'docker://'
checklist.text: Docker refs starting with `docker://` are skipped (not flagged).

checklist.adverse_condition: the action name portion of the uses reference is a dynamic expression
checklist.text: When the action name itself is an expression, skip the reference entirely (no error).

checklist.adverse_condition: the action name is a literal but the version portion of the uses reference is a dynamic expression
checklist.text: When only the version ref is a dynamic expression, flag it with an error indicating the ref is a dynamic expression that cannot be verified for pinning.
The config supports `allowed-owners` field.
The config supports `allowed-actions` field.
The config supports `denied-owners` field.
The config supports `denied-actions` field.
Owner matching is case-insensitive.
Allowed and denied actions use `owner/repo` format.
Global and per-path allowed lists merge by union across matching configurations.
Global and per-path denied lists merge by union across matching configurations.
Denials take precedence over allowances.

checklist.adverse_condition: an action is listed in a denied list
checklist.text: Entries in denied lists are still subject to pinning checks rather than unconditionally blocked.

checklist.adverse_condition: the action appears in the known-actions data and the uses reference uses a mutable version
checklist.text: For popular actions in the known-actions data, error suggestions reference the specific known version.
Per-path overrides use the `action-pinning` key to override the pinning level.

checklist.adverse_condition: there is no global action-pinning config section but there is a per-path override
checklist.text: A per-path entry enables the rule even without a global `action-pinning` section.
An `-action-pinning-level` CLI flag exists.
The `-action-pinning-level` CLI flag overrides only the pinning level (not allow/deny lists).

checklist.adverse_condition: the rule would otherwise be disabled (e.g., action-pinning: null or absent)
checklist.text: The `-action-pinning-level` CLI flag enables the rule even when it would otherwise be disabled.

checklist.text: Config validation rejects invalid level values.

checklist.text: Config validation rejects owners with slashes.

next_advices: Fix 5 test bugs in test/circuit-breaker.test.ts then run vitest to produce execution evidence. checklist.text: A new public helper named createPersisterRestoreResult is exported from query-core.
createPersisterRestoreResult must accept an object with the shape { data, state } as its single argument (non-curried).

The restored query must retain the provided failure counters from the persisted state.

checklist.adverse_condition: observer is mounted after restoration
checklist.text: Restored observer results exposed by supported adapters must reflect the persisted failure count and timestamp metadata instead of recomputing fresh values during mount.

checklist.adverse_condition: a query already exists in memory when bulk restoration occurs
checklist.text: Bulk restoration must reconcile persisted snapshots with queries that already exist in memory.

checklist.adverse_condition: live cache data has newer timestamp but persisted snapshot error has newer timestamp
checklist.text: If the live cache has newer data (higher data freshness timestamp) but the persisted snapshot has newer error metadata (higher error freshness timestamp), the restored query must keep the newer data while also adopting the newer error state so the result remains a refetch error.

checklist.adverse_condition: data freshness and error freshness conflict between live cache and persisted snapshot
checklist.text: Newer data must not be discarded just because the other side (persisted snapshot or live cache) has the newer error timestamp.

checklist.adverse_condition: a persisted snapshot is restored over an existing query in memory
checklist.text: Restoring over an existing query must merge data freshness and error freshness independently instead of replacing the whole query state as a single unit.

The function signature of createPersisterRestoreResult must have exactly two positional properties in its argument: data and state, where data and state are both present in the single object argument.

checklist.text: Restoring from storage must not rewrite the query to a clean success state.

checklist.text: Restoring from storage must not drop page params for infinite queries.

checklist.text: A container type called Validated exists with two concrete subtypes Valid and Invalid.

checklist.adverse_condition: Multiple independent inputs each producing an error
checklist.text: When validating multiple independent inputs, all errors are collected rather than stopping at the first failure.

checklist.adverse_condition: bind invoked on an Invalid instance
checklist.text: The bind method must still short-circuit.
Invalid must store its errors as an immutable tuple.

checklist.adverse_condition: from_failure called with a single error value
checklist.text: The from_failure classmethod must wrap a single error into a 1-tuple so accumulation works uniformly.

checklist.adverse_condition: Two Invalid containers with distinguishable error tuples
checklist.text: When apply combines two Invalid containers, the resulting error tuple must be self's errors concatenated with the other's errors, preserving stable left-to-right order.

checklist.adverse_condition: swap called on an instance Valid(x) with a non-trivial x
checklist.text: The swap method must turn Valid(x) into Invalid((x,)).

checklist.text: The swap method must turn Invalid(errs) into Valid(errs).

Invalid must support structural pattern matching via __match_args__.
Validated must integrate into the library's container interface hierarchy.

checklist.text: Pipe query statements use `|>` operators to chain transformations instead of nested clauses.
Pipe queries start with a standalone `FROM` clause (no preceding SELECT or WITH).
Each subsequent `|>` step occupies its own line at base indentation.
The pipe operator `|>` and its clause keyword share the same line.
The clause body starts on the next line after the pipe operator and clause keyword, indented one level deeper.

checklist.adverse_condition: When the clause type is one that the existing formatter treats as an indented clause (WHERE, SELECT, ORDER BY, AGGREGATE, EXTEND, SET, DROP).
checklist.text: Clause body indentation follows the same indentation pattern the formatter already uses for that clause type in traditional queries.
Clauses that the existing formatter treats as indented clauses (`WHERE`, `SELECT`, `ORDER BY`, `AGGREGATE`, `EXTEND`, `SET`, `DROP`) place their body on a new indented line after the keyword.
Clauses that the existing formatter treats as one-line clauses (`LIMIT`, `JOIN` and its variants, `AS`) keep their content on the same line as the keyword.
`AGGREGATE` in a pipe step has an optional nested `GROUP BY` sub-clause requiring its own indentation level.
`EXTEND` is a pipe-exclusive clause for computed columns.
`SET` is a pipe-exclusive clause for replacing values.
`DROP` is a pipe-exclusive clause for removing columns.
`AS` is a pipe-exclusive clause for naming intermediates.
Pipe queries enclosed in parentheses are formatted as nested subqueries.
Traditional BigQuery formatting remains unchanged when format is applied to non-pipe queries.
